papers.title: Spacetime-Foam Correlations as the Origin of Cosmological-Constant Dark Energy: Their Effects on Cosmological Evolution and Astrophysical Systems
papers.abstract: Wheeler spacetime foam at the Planck scale is characterized by quantum-gravitational fluctuations that create, oscillate, and annihilate microscopic spacetime structures. We model these structures as a Planck-scale lattice using Euclidean quantum gravity on a simplicial complex. Their long-wavelength collective excitations are described by interacting scalar fields, which we call ``foamons,'' in analogy with phonons in a crystal lattice. Through Coleman--Hawking interactions, foamons couple to quantum or classical field operators at scales much larger than the Planck length. These operators provide physical infrared scales that determine the characteristic correlation lengths of the foamon fields. We use a Wilsonian renormalisation-group framework to study their scaling-invariant behaviour near infrared and ultraviolet fixed points. Integrating out the foamon degrees of freedom generates effective actions for physical field operators, with the foamon correlation lengths setting the corresponding macroscopic scales and effective couplings. We apply this framework to cosmology and astrophysics, where the Ricci-scalar sector gives rise to an effective cosmological term $\Lambda_R\sim\xi_R^{-2}$ with equation of state $p_\Lambda\approx -\rho_\Lambda$. For a cosmological correlation length $\xi_R\sim H^{-1}$, this yields $\rho_{\Lambda_R}\sim M_{\rm pl}^2H^2$, providing a possible mechanism for the small observed dark-energy scale. The effective cosmological term $\Lambda_R$ varies in spacetime and interacts with matter through its dependence on the Ricci scalar. We investigate its effects on cosmic evolution, galactic rotation curves, and the deflection of light grazing the solar surface.

papers.title: Non-flat new Tsallis holographic dark energy with the Granda-Oliveros cutoff: DESI DR2 and growth tests
papers.abstract: Holographic dark energy ties the dark-energy density to an infrared length. We study new Tsallis holographic dark energy (NTHDE) with the local Granda-Oliveros (GO) cutoff $L^{-2}=\alpha H^2+\gamma\dot H$ in a curved universe and test it with background and growth data. The background is an autonomous system with exact results. The dark energy splits into a matter-like part, a curvature-like part and an accelerating part. The coefficient of $(1+z)^2$ in $H^2/H_0^2$ is $R_k \Omega_{k0}$ with $R_k>1$, while distances measure $\Omega_{k0}$; the Ricci cutoff gives $R_k=1$. The nucleosynthesis bound and the future fold singularity of the flat model remain valid with curvature. With Pantheon+SH0ES supernovae, cosmic chronometers and DESI DR2 BAO, the model fits slightly better than flat $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\chi^2=-2.82$) and gives a flat universe, $\Omega_{k0}=-0.001^{+0.041}_{-0.043}$. Its Bayesian evidence is comparable to that of $\Lambda$CDM with Union3 supernovae ($\ln B=+0.53$), while $\Lambda$CDM is preferred with Pantheon+SH0ES ($\ln B=-2.66\pm0.24$). The model reproduces the evolution of dark energy preferred by DESI: its effective equation of state has $w_0=-0.88^{+0.11}_{-0.07}$ and $w_a=-0.48^{+0.42}_{-2.15}$ and crosses $-1$ near $z\simeq0.6$, and this comes from the Tsallis deformation. A forecast shows that standard parametrizations recover the curvature of the model without bias, although $R_k$ itself is degenerate with the dark-energy evolution. Linear growth with 18 $f\sigma_8$ data leaves these results unchanged and gives a clear test: if the matter-like part does not cluster, growth is slower, and a CMB-normalised amplitude allows only $\Omega_d^{(m)}\lesssim0.03$.

papers.title: Entropy: the Route from the Gaussian Field to the Statistical Mechanics of the Thermal Radiation
papers.abstract: Maximum Entropy or canonical typicality applied to the electromagnetic field can provide starting points for arriving at the Bose distribution of the photon numbers of thermal radiation, but they rely on statistical postulates whose experimental testability is controversial. Here we start from the experimentally verifiable assumption of Gaussianity of the electromagnetic field. We analyze the field by projecting it onto orthonormal time-frequency basis functions with unitary bandwidth duration product that represent field's orthogonal time-frequency modes. Through the Glauber-Surashdan representation, we see that the joint density operator of the modes in the photon number basis factorize into diagonal density operators with geometric coefficients of individual modes, while the mean photon occupations of the modes remains still unknown. Imposing Clausius' relation on the entropy rates and energy rates of the independent modes we get Bose's mean photon occupancy. Thus, our main claim is that for the first time Bose statistics is obtained under explicit, experimentally verifiable statistical assumptions, without any assumption that is not experimentally verifiable. From the mean occupation numbers, the Boltzmann distribution of the energy of matter particles of the material that generates/absorbes the radiation is then derived by retracing in the backward direction the Einstein-Feynman detailed balance.
